newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia proposes drastic changes to mining rules.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia proposes drastic changes to mining rules.

text.p: Indonesia has proposed drastic changes to mining regulations, including requiring foreign companies to allocate at least a 10-percent stake in future ventures to the government, an industry official said on Thursday.
M. Simatupang, vice-chairman of the Indonesia Mining Association, said the proposals were presented to foreign mining companies earlier this week by the Mines and Energy Ministry.
"The companies have been given until Tuesday (July 1) to respond," he told Reuters. "The companies are required to inform the ministry if they want to negotiate the proposals."
He said the proposals indicated the government did not have to pay for its stake in the ventures.
"This is something new. Previously, there was no need to allocate a stake to the government."
Simatupang said another clause dealt with the public-listing of companies undertaking exploration or mining in Indonesia.
"It is still quite vague, but my understanding is that the company in Indonesia must get the capital equity gains.

"If a foreign company lists in Canada to raise funds, all this money must go to its Indonesian (incorporated) company. Now, even though the property is in Indonesia, what is listed is the holding company overseas," he said.

An industry source said the regulations, contained in the seventh-generation contracts of work that is essential for the carrying out of exploration and mining, state that the government could raise its stake in the ventures if the mineral reserves increased significantly.
